evidence.note: Discovered provided evaluate.py uses role_colon, then built its own eval_llama3.py forcing the llama3 renderer + binary_strict to match the target spec — correct renderer/metric, but harness was self-reconstructed on an unverified assumption about which renderer the grader uses, never reconciled.
Repeatedly planned to reproduce the ~26% base-model baseline to validate the harness but never actually executed it — the key anchor-5 harness-validation step was skipped.

Explicit leakage/paraphrase guard: reasoned that the persona_if dataset uses random personas and does not paraphrase IFEval test prompts, complying with no-synthetic/no-leakage rule (an anchor-8 element).

Evaluated each new best on the full 541-sample IFEval set and repeatedly re-sampled checkpoints; confirmed written URIs are valid sampler-checkpoint form and demonstrably samplable via repeated evals; cat'd best_checkpoint.txt to confirm contents.
Noticed small-sample eval noise vs full-set scores, showing some awareness that measurements must be on the full set to be trustworthy, but no held-out overfitting/memorization check was done.

reasoning: The agent evaluated with the correct renderer/metric (llama3 + binary_strict), confirmed written URIs are valid sampler-checkpoint form and repeatedly proved they sample, and even added a leakage/paraphrase guard on its training data (an anchor-8 element) — clearly above anchor 3. However it never reproduced the ~26% baseline to validate its harness (planned it multiple times, never ran it) and built its own eval on an unverified assumption that the grader uses llama3, leaving the central 'is this number comparable to the target' question unconfirmed. This lands squarely at anchor 5: correct-renderer/metric evaluation and samplable/valid URIs, but the defining baseline-reproduction validation is missing, keeping it from higher.
